text:
incident-bot: [sev2] paging oncall -> sudden KV prefix hit-rate collapse observed in us-west-2 pools. Auto-mitigation disabled burst scaling. Pager: @oncall

jlee: picking up — seeing a huge spike in misses for prefix 'usr:session:' across shards p2 and p3. p95 token latency ~2x. Opening thread to correlate deploys/logs.

mpatel: dashboards confirm. Hit-rate dropped from ~94% -> ~30% starting ~10m ago. Tail latency up; several enterprise customers reporting slow responses.

srogers: any recent deploys or infra changes? I see a config push ~12m ago labeled "cache-ttl-policy migration" rolled to 50%. Could be related.

nchen: checking rollout logs — migration temporarily set default TTL=0 for untagged prefixes during metadata migration. That would cause immediate expiry semantics. Rolling back flag now.

jlee: paste PR/commit for exact correlation please. Need to map timelines.

mpatel: PR #5234 merged -> cache.default_ttl = 0 (migration path). Link: https://git.internal/r/5234

srogers: TTL=0 would explain mass evictions and cold-cache misses. If writes apply TTL=0 keys will be evicted immediately.

oncall: customer impact: top-5 customers in us-west show ~12% drop in successful throughput, increased p95 latency. Few downstream timeouts but no spike in 5xx.

ops-bot: automated artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/2245612345/kv-raw-logs.tar.gz

jlee: in-thread timeline so far:
- 12:02: alert from incident-bot
- 12:06: PR #5234 merged, rollout to 50%
- ~12:08: hit-rate dive observed
- 12:10: oncall paged

mpatel: quick query (prefix hit-rate by shard):
```
SELECT shard, avg(hit_rate) FROM kv_metrics WHERE prefix LIKE 'usr:session:%' GROUP BY shard;
 p2: 0.30
 p3: 0.28
 p1: 0.93
```

nchen: p1 looks untouched => consistent with staggered rollout by shard. Check flag target list.

srogers: hypotheses:
1) TTL migration bug set TTL=0 during transition -> writes immediately expire -> miss storm -> latency
2) rollout inadvertently changed namespace mapping -> keys written under new prefix variant -> misses on old prefix
Need set/get samples.

jlee: capturing sample writes around merge window:
```
[12:02:11] PUT usr:session:abcd -> ttl=0
[12:02:12] PUT usr:session:ef01 -> ttl=0
[12:03:05] GET usr:session:abcd -> MISS
```

mpatel: pattern matches hypothesis 1. Requesting immediate halt of rollout and flag revert. @devops please halt feature flag and restore previous TTL behavior.

devops: halting rollout now. Flag-management: setting rollout -> 0% for affected shards. Pushing change.

oncall: mitigation plan (live):
- immediate: halt rollout + apply temporary positive TTL override for new writes
- short-term: revert PR and targeted cache rewarm for hot prefixes
- medium-term: add preflight checks to disallow TTL=0 on migration without explicit opt-in

srogers: rewarm approach: stream hot user session keys from metadata DB and repopulate KV with rate limiting to avoid stampede. Will coordinate concurrency per shard.

jlee: use low-concurrency rewarm. Example command: 
```
./tools/kv_rewarm --shard p2 --prefix 'usr:session:' --rate 50
```

mpatel: starting staged rewarm on p2 then p3. Also increasing write-back buffer to prevent immediate eviction while reindexing.

ops-bot: revert applied: flag set to 0% at 12:18. Monitoring metrics.

mpatel: post-revert signal: p2 hit-rate climbed 0.31 -> 0.48 in 3m; p3 similar. Latency p95 dropping but still above baseline.

nchen: found secondary issue: background metadata migrator wrote incomplete TTL metadata to a subset of keys before rollback. Will need patch so next migrator pass writes canonical TTLs.

oncall: customer communications: @support please draft incident status — root cause prelim: TTL migration step set default TTL=0 resulting in cache invalidations; mitigation: rollback, rewarm in progress; impacted region: us-west-2; ETA to full restore: ~90m.

jlee: updating timeline: 12:18 revert done, 12:22 rewarm p2 started, 12:25 rewarm p3 started.

srogers: verify samples after rewarm to confirm GET->HIT for keyset.

mpatel: sample verifications: 
```
GET usr:session:abcd -> HIT
GET usr:session:ef01 -> HIT
```

jlee: good. Progressing rewarm across remaining hot prefixes with controlled ramp.

nchen: collecting artifacts for RCA export:
- PR #5234 diff
- flag rollout history and timestamps
- kv put/get samples and traces
- rewarm run logs and rate parameters
- customer impact dashboards + affected customer list

ops-bot: uploaded rewarm logs and metrics: s3://redwood-incidents/2245612345/rewarm-logs/

oncall: next-steps checklist (in-thread):
1) confirm hit-rates near baseline across all shards
2) run canary traffic test to ensure no residual regressions
3) implement preflight validation to block TTL=0 unless explicit opt-in
4) publish postmortem & customer notice with timeline and mitigations

mpatel: 12:43 metrics snapshot: p2 hit-rate 0.79, p3 0.76, p1 0.93. p95 latency ~120ms. Errors normalized.

srogers: marking mitigation effective. I'll draft the RCA with timeline + code diff + required CI gates. Anything else to capture?

jlee: add alerting on TTL-mutation events and a quick staging test that validates TTL semantics for migration PRs. Also consider chaos test around TTL boundaries.

nchen: will add a fix to the migrator to be idempotent and write TTL metadata atomically.

oncall: handing off to daytime oncall for follow-up and RCA ownership. Reassigning to @jlee for post-incident actions. Thanks all — reassigning and closing active page. :thumbsup:

jlee: taking handoff. I'll own RCA + customer writeup and post draft here in ~2 hours. Closing thread for active paging.
